findings.title: x
findings.message: Every accepted step runs two full modal analyses. Each analysis performs `count` dense MNA solves, allocating a fresh `size×size` matrix per column, plus a complex eigendecomposition and `count` complex solves to invert the eigenvector matrix. Each `transientLCProposal` call also rescans every authored component through `usesModalLCCeiling`. For long transients with a small output step, this can dominate the Radau work and push runs into the work/time guard. The example limitation text already warns that the guard may be reached.
findings.suggestion: Cache `usesModalLCCeiling()` on the network. Reuse one Jacobian scratch buffer across columns. Consider skipping the midpoint analysis when the endpoint ceiling is well above `h`, or re-evaluating the modal ceiling only every few steps or when the step ratio changes significantly.
findings.evidence:
middle := n.transientLCCeiling(half, trace, at+h/2, budget)
			nextCeiling = n.transientLCCeiling(refined, trace, at+h, budget)

findings.title: Modal Jacobian validity is logged but never asserted
findings.message: The validity flags from storageJacobian and checkedOscillationRate are only logged. If modal analysis silently fails for the Class-AB example, the code falls back to the legacy ceiling and the test still passes. That means it does not guard the feature it is meant to exercise.
findings.suggestion: Assert `ok && good`, and assert that `state.net.usesModalLCCeiling()` is true, so this test fails when the modal path is not taken.
findings.evidence:
a, ok := state.net.storageJacobian(stage, trace, 0, budget)
	rate, good := checkedOscillationRate(a)
	t.Log("state Jacobian", a, "valid", ok, good, "rate", rate, "old ceiling", state.net.maximumInductorStep(), "new ceiling", state.net.transientLCCeiling(stage, trace, 0, budget))

fix.before:

	rate, good := checkedOscillationRate(a)
	t.Log("state Jacobian", a, "valid", ok, good, "rate", rate, "old ceiling", state.net.maximumInductorStep(), "new ceiling", state.net.transientLCCeiling(stage, trace, 0, budget))

findings.title: Test claims positive outputs without checking them
findings.message: The test name and log message claim it produces positive outputs. The loop only checks for errors, work bounds and conservation, and it never inspects the speaker output values. A regression that produces zero or wrong-signed output would still pass.
findings.suggestion: Assert on `state.result.Speakers[0].Voltage` or `.Current`, for example require a nonzero positive voltage after the first few samples. Alternatively, rename the test so it does not claim output verification.

finding.title: Exact float equality on accumulated simulation time
finding.message: The parity test compares the simulated time to `.0001` with exact equality. The step is integrated adaptively and the time is built by summing sub-intervals. Accumulated floating-point rounding (e.g. 0.0001 as a sum of halves or quarters plus a remainder) can produce a value a few ULPs away. That makes the test brittle, or causes it to fail on harmless solver changes.
finding.suggestion: Compare with a tolerance, e.g. `math.Abs(a.Mixed.Time-.0001) > 1e-12`, and add the `math` import.
